body:
Just an update on this, *the impact is more significant* than what is described in the issue body.

After you move (or rename) the unique node, if you then try to add a new keyframe to the track using the key icon in the inspector, Godot will create an entirely new track, using the unique node path, **conflicting with the old track**.

The problem as a diff.  This is what happens after I name AvoidanceShape1 to AvoidanceShape12, then click the key icon on AvoidanceShape12's rotation property.  I now have two tracks referencing the same node, but they're kept separate in the animation player.
```diff
--- a/assets/animations/player_character/moves/reacting/reacting_jumppad_providing/reacting_jumppad_providing.tres
+++ b/assets/animations/player_character/moves/reacting/reacting_jumppad_providing/reacting_jumppad_providing.tres
@@ -186,7 +186,7 @@ tracks/14/keys = {
 tracks/15/type = "value"
 tracks/15/imported = false
 tracks/15/enabled = true
-tracks/15/path = NodePath("%AvoicanceBox/AvoidanceShape1:shape:size")
+tracks/15/path = NodePath("../AvoicanceBox/AvoidanceShape12:shape:size")
 tracks/15/interp = 1
 tracks/15/loop_wrap = true
 tracks/15/keys = {
@@ -198,7 +198,7 @@ tracks/15/keys = {
 tracks/16/type = "value"
 tracks/16/imported = false
 tracks/16/enabled = true
-tracks/16/path = NodePath("%AvoicanceBox/AvoidanceShape1:position")
+tracks/16/path = NodePath("../AvoicanceBox/AvoidanceShape12:position")
 tracks/16/interp = 1
 tracks/16/loop_wrap = true
 tracks/16/keys = {
@@ -221,3 +221,15 @@ tracks/17/keys = {
 "method": &"progress_to_next_frame"
 }]
 }
+tracks/18/type = "value"
+tracks/18/imported = false
+tracks/18/enabled = true
+tracks/18/path = NodePath("%AvoicanceBox/AvoidanceShape12:rotation")
+tracks/18/interp = 1
+tracks/18/loop_wrap = true
+tracks/18/keys = {
+"times": PackedFloat32Array(0),
+"transitions": PackedFloat32Array(1),
+"update": 0,
+"values": [Vector3(0, 0, 0)]
+}
```
